n_welcome.assistantText:
Hi — I’ll ask a few short questions to suggest the right level of care. I’m not your doctor, and this isn’t a diagnosis.

Tap Continue when you’re ready.

n_gate.assistantText:
First, is anything on this list happening right now?

Tap one answer below. If more than one fits, choose what worries you most.

options.label: Confusion, very hard to wake, seizure, or a bad head injury with confusion
Heavy bleeding, repeated vomiting of blood, coughing a lot of blood, or black tarry stools
Severe trouble breathing, choking feeling, or blue/gray lips or fingertips

n_age.assistantText: What age group are you in?

n_sex.assistantText: How do you describe your sex? (We only use this to tailor a few questions.)

n_onset.assistantText: How long has your main symptom been going on?

options.label: Cold, cough, sore throat, or flu-like illness
Fever, chills, or feeling burning hot without mainly cold symptoms
Weakness, numbness, trouble speaking, or face droop
Burning urine, flank pain, or suspected UTI
Rash, hives, or skin infection concern
Injury, fall, or new severe pain after trauma
Anxiety, panic, low mood, or scary thoughts

n_cold_fev.assistantText: Do you have a real fever, hard chills, or body aches that really wipe you out?

n_cold_breath.assistantText: Are you short of breath when you rest, or does your chest feel tight with each breath?

n_cold_coughblood.assistantText: Are you coughing up more than a little streak of blood?

n_skin_gate.assistantText: Is the rash spreading fast, or do you have fever with a stiff neck or confusion along with the rash?

n_skin_face.assistantText: Is the rash near your eye, or are there painful blisters in a stripe on one side of your face or body?

n_mh_harm.assistantText: I need to ask this plainly: are you thinking about hurting yourself or someone else?

n_mh_panic.assistantText: Does it come in waves — pounding heart, shaking, a strong fear something awful is happening — then ease after a little while?

n_fever_temp.assistantText: Do you feel burning hot or have hard chills — or a temperature about 39°C / 102°F or higher if you checked?

n_fever_days.assistantText: How long have you felt this way?

n_chest_sob.assistantText: Even at rest, are you short of breath, or too winded to finish a short sentence?

n_chest_radiate.assistantText: Does the pain spread to your arm, jaw, neck, or back — especially with sweating or an upset stomach?

n_chest_exert.assistantText: Does walking fast, climbing stairs, or stress bring it on, or does it feel like heavy squeezing across your chest?

n_breath_severe.assistantText: Right now, is it very hard to breathe — for example blue lips or fingers, you’re working hard to pull air in, or you can’t walk a few steps?

n_breath_duration.assistantText: How long have breathing symptoms lasted?

n_neuro_face.assistantText: Is one side of your face drooping, or is your smile uneven?

n_neuro_arm.assistantText: Did numbness, weakness, or trouble speaking start suddenly on one side?

n_gi_blood.assistantText: Any black tarry stools, throwing up blood, or a lot of bleeding from the rectum?

n_gi_pain.assistantText: Is the belly pain the worst you’ve ever had, or spread out with a board-hard belly?

n_gi_fluids.assistantText: Have you kept almost no fluids down for more than about 8 hours, or made very little urine?

n_uri_fever.assistantText: Along with burning or frequent urine — do you have fever, side pain, nausea, or vomiting?

n_inj_severe.assistantText: After the injury: bad confusion, repeated vomiting, or you can’t use a limb?

n_head_thunder.assistantText: Did this headache hit like a thunderclap — the worst ever — or come with vision changes or weakness?

n_smoking.assistantText: Do you smoke cigarettes or vape nicotine most days?

n_alcohol.assistantText: Do you drink more than about 8 drinks a week (women) or 15 (men), or often binge?

n_immuno.assistantText: Are you on chemotherapy, daily steroid pills (such as prednisone), or other medicines that strongly suppress immunity (as prescribed by a specialist)?

n_preg.assistantText: Could you be pregnant, maybe pregnant, or within six weeks after giving birth?

t_em_global_neuro.careSummary: Your answers describe possible severe neurological or head-injury symptoms. Call your local emergency number or go to the nearest emergency department now.
hintBullets: Do not drive yourself if confused or drowsy.
If someone is with you, ask them to stay nearby.

t_em_global_bleed.careSummary: Heavy bleeding or signs of significant internal bleeding need urgent in-person care. Call emergency services or go to the ER.
hintBullets: Lie down if you feel faint; avoid alcohol and blood-thinning medicines unless a clinician told you to take them.

t_emergency_skin.careSummary: A rapidly spreading rash with fever, stiff neck, or confusion can be serious. Seek emergency care now.
hintBullets: Note when the rash started and any new medicines — bring a list if you can.

t_emergency_crisis.careSummary: If you may harm yourself or others, seek immediate help. Call your local emergency number, or in the U.S. call or text 988 (Suicide & Crisis Lifeline). Go to the nearest emergency department if you cannot stay safe.
hintBullets: You are not alone — crisis lines are staffed 24/7.
Remove access to anything you might use to hurt yourself if you can do so safely.

t_emergency_chest.careSummary: Your answers suggest possible serious heart or lung involvement. If symptoms are severe or worsening, call your local emergency number or go to the nearest emergency department now.
hintBullets: Do not drive yourself if you feel faint, sweaty, or short of breath.
Chew aspirin only if previously advised by a clinician; otherwise seek care first.

t_emergency_breath.careSummary: Severe breathing difficulty needs urgent in-person assessment. Call emergency services or go to the ER.
hintBullets: Sit upright, loosen tight clothing, and use any prescribed rescue inhaler only as directed.

t_emergency_stroke.careSummary: Possible stroke symptoms are time-critical. Call emergency services immediately — note the time symptoms started.
hintBullets: Do not eat or drink until evaluated.
Have someone stay with you if possible.

t_emergency_gi.careSummary: Bleeding or severe abdominal symptoms need urgent evaluation. Seek emergency care.
hintBullets: Avoid NSAIDs until evaluated if bleeding is suspected.

t_emergency_injury.careSummary: Significant injury or head symptoms after trauma need urgent assessment. Go to the ER or call emergency services.
hintBullets: Immobilize the injured area; avoid moving if neck pain after trauma.

t_emergency_head.careSummary: Sudden severe headache with neurological symptoms needs emergency evaluation.
hintBullets: Rest in a dark quiet room while awaiting care if advised by dispatch.

t_computed.careSummary: Based on your answers, use the guidance below. When in doubt, seek in-person care.
hintBullets: This tool cannot diagnose or prescribe.
A licensed clinician should review persistent or worsening symptoms.
